title: Retrieval with an authorization boundary
summary: An internal knowledge assistant with department-scoped retrieval, hybrid search, streaming responses, and evaluation.
decision: Enforce department permissions in retrieval, alongside authentication and output handling.

study.problem: A shared knowledge assistant must answer useful questions without retrieving documents the current user is not allowed to read.
study.built: Built a RAG application with JWT authentication, Redis token revocation and conversation memory, department-scoped retrieval, BM25/vector search, cross-encoder reranking, and streaming responses.
study.architecture: Requests pass through authentication, per-user rate limits, and input checks. Retrieval filters accessible namespaces before reranking. Redis stores conversation state and revoked tokens. Output handling includes PII redaction; optional Llama Guard adds another safety check.

decisions.title: Authorize before generation
decisions.body: Department access is enforced at retrieval rather than relying on instructions to the model or a hidden UI control.

decisions.title: Measure the full question set
decisions.body: The 25-question evaluation scored 0.9116 faithfulness. The 50-question run scored 0.7423 with a different judge model. Both belong in the results.

decisions.title: Separate evaluation from tests
decisions.body: Automated tests cover retrieval, Redis, re-ingestion, and guardrails. They are distinct from the question sets used to evaluate answer quality.

results.label: 50-question faithfulness
results.context: Full recorded evaluation using llama-3.1-8b-instant for scoring; answer relevancy 0.6495.

results.label: 25-question faithfulness
results.context: Subset evaluated using llama-3.3-70b-versatile; answer relevancy 0.7346. Different samples and judges prevent a direct comparison.

study.limitations: Model-judged scores depend on the question set and judge. Pattern-based guardrails and optional model checks do not establish comprehensive security or production readiness.
study.lesson: The authorization boundary and evaluation conditions matter more than a single headline score.
